newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares hang on U.S. rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares hang on U.S. rate rise.

text.p: The test for investors in the Belgian market will be at what level the Federal Open Market Committee, the policy-making arm of the Federal Reserve, sets interest rates on Tuesday, dealers said.
Market sentiment is that if the Fed hikes rates above 25 basis-points this will spark a major sell-off in shares.

"People were on the sidelines today and will wait for the FOMC's decision. A 25 points rise is anticipated and good news but if it's higher then it's dangerous for both the bond and the stock market," said a trader at a major Belgian bank.
Brussels Bel-20 closed up 1.06 percent at 2,106.18.
The blue-chip Bel-20 saw a dull trading day, with most dealers putting it down to a wait-and-see policy among investors eager to get direction from the U.S. and Wall Street.
"It's been extemely quiet today, only really busy at opening and closing," said another dealer.
Analysts and dealers in Belgium said the market had already taken into account a 25 basis-points rise, adding that if this came true Wednesday would not see a major correction in the market.
"A 25 basis-points rise has already been taken into account in recent falls," said a dealer.
FOMC is due to announce the results of its deliberations after 1900 GMT.

Among Bel-20 movers much attention was on holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) as speculation mounted that its majority shareholder French Cie de Suez is set to merge with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
Suez has a 63 percent stake in SGB. SGB closed up 3.02 percent at 2,895 francs.
Elsewhere eyes were on insurer Fortis AG gaining 2.04 percent to 5,990 francs supported by expectations that it will announce a 16 percent increase in 1996 net profit.

Utility holding company Electrabel, which fell 0.77 percent on Monday after the government announced it would see the tax on its profits rise to 14 percent from 12 percent, recovered to close up 1.67 percent at 7,900 francs.
Market players were also eyeing 1996 results from electronics group Barco, Electrafina, and retailers Delhaize and GIB which are due on Wednesday after the bourse closes.
